correctness.rationale: Exact center-chord radial length follows algebraically from both cylinder inequalities and unit direction normalization. Polar spherical Jacobian 1/(4pi) and eight azimuth sectors yield a finite integral; its t derivative is an elementary arctangent and matching t=1/sqrt(2) establishes the closed CDF. Chain differentiation yields the positive density. Taylor expansions at both endpoints give normalized coefficients. Four near-maximal diagonal lobes satisfy an exact trigonometric inequality; \(q/h,z/\sqrt h\) map their uniform spherical conditional measures onto bounded domains with indicators converging in L1 to \(2|a|+b^2<1\). Their area \(4/3\) gives density \(3/4\), uniform label, and total-variation convergence. An independently coded numerical script verifies 440041 finite diagnostics but does not replace the proof.

value.rationale: An exactly solvable entire central-chord law for a classical non-smooth convex intersection is a natural metric-statistics classification not supplied by its elementary volume/area invariants. The different endpoint exponents and two-scale parabolic four-lobe conditional limit expose how extremal orientations govern a measurable rare event. The marked law offers more structural information than scalar CDF or a tabulated isolated constant and is a motivated target for geometric sampling and stereology.
